question: Cross-project orchestration safety — does F005a/F006/F008 protect against process-global state contamination across parallel agents?
answer: No. Critical gap. Tools like gcloud (~/.config/gcloud), firebase (~/.config/configstore), kubectl (~/.kube), gh (~/.config/gh), npm (~/.npmrc), docker (~/.docker), gradle (~/.gradle), android, terraform — all maintain process-global mutable state. `gcloud config set project X` in one agent contaminates every other agent on the machine. Codex audit caught this. Adding F023 now (before any cross-project work) with EC1-EC13. EC10 originally scoped CLOUDSDK_CONFIG-only; Codex re-audit corrected to per-supervisor ExecutionEnvironment generalized across all tools (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, KUBECONFIG, GH_CONFIG_DIR, NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG, DOCKER_CONFIG, GRADLE_USER_HOME, ANDROID_USER_HOME, TF_DATA_DIR + tool-specific flag discipline for xcodebuild/gradle).
rationale: EC10 (ExecutionEnvironment isolation via per-tool namespace env vars) is the architectural keystone — it makes mutations sandboxed so parallel supervisors are safe even if agents disregard prompt discipline. EC9 (forbid mutating commands) is belt-and-suspenders. EC4 (env var injection) protects READS. Together: defense in depth. Without F023, parallel agents on Glam + SpinDine + Jarvis would silently contaminate each other's gcloud/firebase/kubectl/etc state. Hard block on F009-F014 + any production deploy automation until at least EC9 + EC10-generalized green. F006/F007/F008 can proceed Jarvis-local since they don't dispatch agent commands against cloud projects.

question: F023 Step 2 — scope expansion record: EC2-only proposed → EC2 + EC7 approved. What landed, what stays deferred?
answer: Scope expansion: original Step 2 slice was EC2 alone. Mid-turn the agent surfaced an explicit EC2-only vs EC2+EC7 cost delta (EC2 ≈ 45-60 min; EC2+EC7 ≈ 75 min, EC7 piggybacks the same validator seam). User approved the bundle before any code was written; the locked AC was rewritten before implementation. Step 2 lands EC2 (plan-level Target contract) and EC7 (prod gate). EC2: new module plan_target.py exposes parse_target_section + validate_prod_gates + normalize_target_project; plans must declare a visible `## Target` block with target_env in {dev,staging,prod} and target_project (a string, with the `none` sentinel allowed for host-local plans). plan_loader.load() invokes the parser + validator and exposes LoadedPlan.target_env (str) + LoadedPlan.target_project (str | None — sentinel normalized to None). supervisor.dispatch_single_agent and dispatch_volley default target_env/target_project from the loaded plan when kwargs are unset; explicit kwargs override and are recorded as target_source=kwarg vs target_source=plan in audit validation_performed. EC7: validate_prod_gates rejects target_env=prod plans missing pre_impl + on_escalation in human_gates (PROD_REQUIRED_GATES). Backfill: parent plan + 2026-04-25-001 firebase-bootstrap got target_project=jarvis-a6ee1; 2026-04-25-002 trivial-orchestration-test got target_project=none; synthetic test fixtures in test_volley_synthetic.py and test_execution_environment.py also got Target sections. 17 new tests in tests/test_plan_target.py.
rationale: Why expand: EC7 is a single additional rule on the same validator that EC2 introduces — splitting would force a near-identical re-touch of plan_target.py and plan_loader.py within a week and lose the prod-safety story. Why this scope expansion was acceptable under the agent process rule: the agent did not silently expand; it surfaced the EC2-only vs EC2+EC7 delta with explicit cost numbers and a recommendation, and waited for approval before locking the AC. Why the env-var override pattern: matches the existing convention (notify.DISABLE_ENV) and keeps the module attribute GLOBAL_HISTORY_PATH assignable for legacy callers. Why an autouse conftest fixture rather than per-test setup: eliminates the chance of forgetting isolation in a future real-volley test; tmp_path is per-test so no cross-leak. Why the resume_all gate_pause bug needed the cli-layer fix to land: cli._resume_main called resume_all with declared=[] which short-circuited at the if not newly check; without unblocking the resume_all path, the cli-layer valid_targets fix would still leave active_breakers stuck. Why budget_ceiling restricts to participating agents: the F020 quota_state.json is global per-agent — without restriction, a long-tail Claude over-quota would trip every volley including a Codex-only one. Restricting to agents that actually have audits in the current volley keeps the breaker scoped to the current dispatch. Test pollution risk acknowledged from the start of F006 (record_global_hit always wrote to ~/.jarvis/) but the threshold (3 iteration_cap hits in 24h) made the cascade non-deterministic; only surfaced when running the full sweep on a 24h-old polluted operator file.

question: F006 second-pass review surfaced 5 more honesty/correctness gaps after ea3d68b - fix inline?
answer: Yes. Five fixes under the same small-correctness-fix exception. (1) Active breaker:* gates now preempt _resolve_executor in supervisor.dispatch_volley. The gate-pause evaluation block was below executor resolution; an active breaker:wall_clock with empty AGENT_REGISTRY raised KeyError instead of returning paused_on_gate. Moved the entire gate-pause check (declared_gates evaluation, INBOX gate_hit event, notify, paused_on_gate return) to the line BEFORE _resolve_executor, joining the global-breaker check that already preempted resolution. New regression test test_active_breaker_preempts_executor_resolution clears AGENT_REGISTRY, plants breaker:wall_clock, asserts result.final_status == paused_on_gate. (2) Test-suite invocation guidance corrected: every test module docstring used to say `python -m jarvis_orchestrate.tests.<mod>` which bypasses the conftest autouse fixture and writes to the operator's real ~/.jarvis/. Replaced all 11 docstrings with `pytest scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/<mod>.py`. The conftest fixture is now the only sanctioned entry point. (3) active_supervisors.jsonl pollution: extended the conftest autouse fixture to also set JARVIS_ACTIVE_SUPERVISORS_PATH to per-test tmp_path; added _effective_registry_path() helper in active_supervisors.py mirroring the breaker-history pattern. EC13 _redirect_registry now sets BOTH env var and module attribute so existing assertions on aS.REGISTRY_PATH.read_text() still work. Verified post-sweep: ~/.jarvis/active_supervisors.jsonl no longer created. (4) cli._approve_main now refuses `jarvis approve <plan-id> breaker:global_circuit_breaker` with exit code 2 and a REFUSED message pointing operator at the 24h history window. The global breaker is hard-stop per F006 spec; it has no clearance path. Also tightened breaker_names to {f'breaker:{k.value}' for k in cb.APPROVAL_BREAKERS} (was BreakerKind, which incorrectly included the global). New regression test test_cli_approve_refuses_global_breaker. Sandbox repro confirmed: exit=2, 'REFUSED ... hard-stop'. (5) gate_pause.approve_gate is now genuinely idempotent for breaker:* gates. The previous implementation stripped the breaker from cleared_gates after approval, so a second approve found 'not in cleared_gates' and re-ran the entire flow, appending another approve history entry. New code splits the contract: breaker:* idempotency is governed by active_breakers (no-op when not active); plan-declared gates remain governed by cleared_gates. New regression test test_breaker_approve_is_idempotent: first approve True, second/third approve False, history holds exactly one approve entry. Regression: 128 tests pass (was 125 + 3 new), no pollution to operator ~/.jarvis/.
rationale: Why the gate-pause move was deferred to amend2 rather than caught in amend1: amend1 only moved the global breaker check; the reviewer correctly noted that ANY approval-required breaker faces the same KeyError-shadows-paused_on_gate issue, just less obviously because the global breaker is the more-cited spec line. The review-driven discovery here is exactly why the AC for '6 produce pause-and-resume behavior' specifies executor independence. Why refuse global breaker approve rather than silent-clear: the spec is unambiguous (no clearance path), and silent-clearing risks operators believing they have a recovery lever they do not have. Hard refusal with operator-visible message is the safer surface. Why split the idempotency contract by gate kind rather than tracking a unified 'approved' set: F006 transient breaker lifecycle (re-trip pauses again, after first approve clears) is intentional and tested; if cleared_gates kept breakers, the second trip would not pause. The split keeps both contracts intact: durable for plan-declared gates, transient for breakers, and idempotent for both. Why update all 11 test docstrings, not just F006: the reviewer flagged F006 specifically but every module shares the same conftest fixture; documenting an unsafe entry point on any of them invites the same pollution next time someone follows the docstring. Single sweep is cheaper than per-incident fixes.

question: F007 Slice 2 — what shipped at the locked admission-policy scope, what's deferred, and is F007 ready to flip?
answer: Yes. F007 closes to passes:true at the revised lock (admission policy, not allocation). Two new modules: scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/quota_admission.py defines DispatchClass enum (P0|INTERACTIVE|AUTONOMOUS — runtime classification, NOT a plan.tier overload), classify_dispatch with precedence (mode_override > JARVIS_RUN_MODE env > plan.tier=p0 > autonomous), DeferKind enum (QUOTA_THRESHOLD|INTERACTIVE_BACKOFF), evaluate_quota_threshold reading ~/.jarvis/quota_state.json against JARVIS_QUOTA_DEFER_THRESHOLD (default 70.0% — code constant + env override only, no schema bump), evaluate_interactive_backoff scoped to claude-only when claude is in agents_required, top-level evaluate() returning AdmissionCheck (class, quota check, interactive check, computed active gate set). scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/interactive_state.py wraps ~/.jarvis/interactive_state.json with touch/last_human_request_at/is_within_backoff, honors JARVIS_INTERACTIVE_BACKOFF_MINUTES (default 30) for the window. gate_pause.py extended: parallel active_defers field alongside active_breakers; add_defer + active_defers reader + reconcile_defers helper that diffs desired set vs current and emits defer_trip/defer_clear history events; approve_gate splits idempotency contract three ways (cleared_gates for plan-declared, active_breakers for breaker:*, active_defers for defer:* — transient for both); resume_all clears all three sets. supervisor.dispatch_volley wires admission reconcile after global-breaker check and BEFORE gate-pause + executor resolution: derives plan_tier_str from plan.tier enum, calls quota_admission.evaluate, calls gate_pause.reconcile_defers with computed gate set + reasons map, emits INBOX defer_tripped/defer_cleared events for added/removed deferrals, fires terminal-notifier on each new defer. dispatch_volley signature gains mode kwarg threaded from cli.py's --mode flag (interactive|autonomous|p0). cli.py adds claude-touch subcommand writing interactive_state.json, --mode argparse choice on volley path, approve/resume recognize defer:* names alongside breaker:* (valid_targets unions plan.human_gates + active_breakers + active_defers + APPROVAL_BREAKERS + DeferKind names; global breaker still refused per D074-amend2). conftest.py extended: per-test tmp_path redirects JARVIS_BREAKER_HISTORY_PATH (F006), JARVIS_ACTIVE_SUPERVISORS_PATH (EC13), JARVIS_INTERACTIVE_STATE_PATH (F007), JARVIS_QUOTA_STATE_PATH (F006/F007/F020) — full hermetic isolation. circuit_breakers._read_quota_state and supervisor._read_quota_state both honor JARVIS_QUOTA_STATE_PATH so F006 budget_ceiling, F020 quota_gate, and F007 admission all share the same isolated tmp file in tests. Tests: 14 in test_f007_quota_admission.py covering classify_dispatch precedence, quota threshold default + env override, interactive backoff window + claude scope, all 6 AC scenarios (autonomous/p0-bypass/interactive-bypass for both gates, auto-clear), defer:* idempotency contract, resume_all coverage, claude-touch CLI roundtrip, and approve no-false-warning. Regression: 142 tests pass (was 128 + 14 new), no pollution to ~/.jarvis/. 11 of 23 features signed off (added F007 — Phase 2 capstone).
rationale: Why admission, not allocation, for this slice: F006/F007 cleanly split the work — F006 detects runaway loops AFTER they start; F007 prevents kicking off NEW autonomous work when conditions are unfavorable. Cross-plan allocation accounting requires a global tier-budget tracker (out of scope; would need F-something Slice 3+). Naming the synthetic gates defer:* rather than reusing breaker:* per the lock: dashboards and operator mental models distinguish 'this loop is misbehaving' (breaker) from 'this dispatch shouldn't even start right now' (defer). Why no schema bump for defer_threshold: the lock explicitly held off — env-only keeps Slice 2 small and lets a future v1.4 schema bump add per-plan overrides if needed. Why p0 bypasses BOTH gates per the clarification: p0 is the operator's emergency lane; quota threshold blocking it would defeat the purpose. interactive bypass is symmetric — operator is actively driving and quota state is informational. Why F006-style transient lifecycle (vs sticky approve-with-exemption): keeps the state model simple and preserves the F006 trade-off acknowledged in D074-amend2 (approve is weak against persistent conditions; operator escapes are wait, --mode interactive, or class p0). The simpler model also avoids needing 'last condition transition' tracking. Why redirect JARVIS_QUOTA_STATE_PATH in the autouse fixture: discovered during F007 wiring that real-volley tests were reading the operator's actual quota_state.json (which had claude at ~80%) and tripping defer:quota_threshold in unrelated tests — same class of pollution as F006's breaker_history fix in D074-amend. Adding it to the autouse fixture closes the cross-feature isolation gap proactively. Why force_auditor_signed_off in p0/interactive bypass tests: when admission lets dispatch through, the volley needs to actually complete; without forcing a terminal status the auditor synthetic returns ad-hoc and the test's expected non-paused_on_gate result can be confusing. Forcing signed_off is the smallest-correctness path. Explicitly NOT in this slice (per the lock): cross-plan tier-budget accounting (true 20/10/50/20 reservation), per-plan defer_threshold schema field, auto-detection of human Claude requests via Claude Code hook integration, claude-untouch / TTL CLI. Phase 2 of the parent plan now closes at 11/23 signed off; F022 (OSS Readiness) is the natural next slice.

question: F007 post-merge audit surfaced 4 honesty/correctness issues + 1 missing E2E test case — fix inline?
answer: Yes. Five fixes under the same small-correctness-fix exception. (1) Stale pause-marker bug: gate_pause._maybe_clear_pause_marker() was checking pending pause_gates only against cleared_gates, but transient breaker:* / defer:* gates intentionally don't accumulate there. After approving a defer (or breaker), paused_at + pause_gates would remain stale on disk even though evaluate() correctly ignored them. Rewrote _maybe_clear_pause_marker to consider lifecycle by name prefix: plan-declared resolved iff in cleared_gates; breaker:* resolved iff NOT in active_breakers; defer:* resolved iff NOT in active_defers. Also wired _maybe_clear_pause_marker into reconcile_defers so auto-clearing the last pending defer (without operator action) drops the marker too. (2) F007 admission was wired into dispatch_volley() only; dispatch_single_agent had no admission path even though CLI accepted --mode for both. Wired admission into dispatch_single_agent: same reconcile against quota_state.json + interactive_state.json, agents=['claude'] since F004 hardcodes ClaudeCLIExecutor, gate-pause check before executor resolution, raises new PausedOnGate exception (single-agent dispatch returns Path on success, so exception is the right signal for the pause case). cli single-agent path threads --mode and translates PausedOnGate → exit 3. (3) CLI '[approve] remaining unmet gates' line was using gate_pause.unmet_gates() which considers only plan-declared gates — operator could be told (none) while a transient defer/breaker was still active. Switched to gate_pause.evaluate(plan_dir, declared_strs).unmet which unions plan-declared + active_breakers + active_defers. (4) Backoff expiry was unit-tested only. Added test_e2e_interactive_backoff_expires_auto_clear: dispatch 1 with 15-min-old touch → defer:interactive_backoff active; dispatch 2 after touch ages to 35 min → reconcile auto-clears + dispatch proceeds + INBOX defer_cleared event recorded. Mirrors the existing AC #6 quota-threshold-drop test for the backoff axis. (5) Wording fix in summary: F022 is the next pending feature, not the final pending feature — 11/23 still leaves 12 unsigned (most are Phase 3+). Tests: 5 new (test_pause_marker_clears_when_only_defer_was_pending, test_pause_marker_clears_via_reconcile_auto_remove, test_dispatch_single_agent_pauses_on_quota_threshold, test_cli_approve_remaining_unmet_includes_active_defers, test_e2e_interactive_backoff_expires_auto_clear). Regression: 147 pass (was 142 + 5). No pollution to ~/.jarvis/.
rationale: Why _maybe_clear_pause_marker rewrite is the right shape rather than tracking everything in cleared_gates: F006 (D074) already established that breakers must be transient — adding them to cleared_gates would defeat the re-trip-on-reappearance contract. The marker logic is the only place that needed to know about lifecycle, so the lifecycle dispatch lives there cleanly. Why dispatch_single_agent gets full admission rather than 'volley-only' documentation: the CLI already accepted --mode for both branches; documenting volley-only would require either silently ignoring --mode in single-agent (broken UX) or rejecting it (worse). Wiring admission keeps the contract uniform across entry points. PausedOnGate as a new exception type (instead of returning a sentinel Path or None): dispatch_single_agent's success contract is Path-returning; introducing a second return type would break call sites. RuntimeError subclass with a structured message keeps the exception path narrow. Why use evaluate().unmet for the approve remaining-unmet output rather than a new helper: evaluate() already does the right union; adding a helper would duplicate logic. The unmet_gates() helper stays because it has a narrower contract callers may still want. Why E2E backoff expiry test mirrors AC #6 instead of being its own scenario: the AC wording specifically calls out 'After threshold drop OR 30 min elapsed' as a single bullet — the auto-clear path through reconcile is shared; the missing leg was just covering the time axis explicitly. Test parity is more honest than relying on 'should also work the same way' inference.

question: F007 second-pass review: P0 was reachable via --mode p0 and JARVIS_RUN_MODE=p0, expanding the lock's 'P0 is plan-derived only' framing. Tighten or amend?
answer: Tighten. The original lock said: 'p0 ← plan.tier == "p0" (existing schema, unchanged); interactive ← --mode interactive or JARVIS_RUN_MODE=interactive; autonomous ← default.' My initial implementation drifted: classify_dispatch accepted any DispatchClass value via mode_override or env, so a non-P0 plan could be force-promoted to P0 (bypassing both admission gates). features.json description was correct; only the implementation drifted. Three fixes: (1) Added _OVERRIDE_VALUES = frozenset({INTERACTIVE.value, AUTONOMOUS.value}) and gated mode_override/env lookup against it. mode_override='p0' or JARVIS_RUN_MODE=p0 now silently falls through to the next precedence rule (plan.tier check), preserving plan-derived P0 while denying CLI/env force-promotion. (2) cli.py argparse choices on --mode tightened to ['interactive', 'autonomous'] only — argparse rejects --mode p0 at parse time with exit code 2. (3) Updated --mode help text to call out the constraint explicitly. Tests: 2 new — test_p0_is_plan_derived_only_not_overridable asserts that mode_override='p0' on a non-P0 plan stays AUTONOMOUS, env JARVIS_RUN_MODE=p0 same, and that plan-derived P0 still works (legitimate path); test_cli_mode_argparse_rejects_p0 invokes cli.main with --mode p0 and asserts argparse exit=2 with 'invalid choice' / 'p0' in stderr. Regression: 149 pass (was 147 + 2). features.json description needed no change — it already correctly described the precedence per the lock; only the implementation had drifted.
rationale: Why tighten rather than amend the lock to allow forced-P0: emergency-lane semantics belong with the plan-author, not the operator at dispatch time. A plan author who declares tier=p0 has thought about whether the work justifies bypassing admission gates; an operator running `jarvis-orchestrate --mode p0` has not necessarily done so. Allowing CLI/env P0 promotion silently expands the surface where quota threshold + interactive backoff stop applying, which is the exact behavior the lock guarded against. interactive mode override is different — operator is actively driving and can self-throttle; autonomous is the safe default. P0 sits between them as a 'this work is important enough to ignore guards' lane, and that judgment call is heavier than --mode is meant to carry. Why fall-through-silently rather than raise on 'p0' override: matches argparse's choice rejection behavior at the library boundary — if a programmatic caller passes 'p0' with the assumption it works, the function returns the tier-derived result (which is the correct behavior for that caller's plan); raising would surface a class of error that's already caught upstream by argparse. Why argparse choice restriction is belt-and-suspenders with the library guard: defense in depth — CLI users get a clear error at parse time ('invalid choice: p0'); programmatic callers (tests, hypothetical future supervisor wrappers) hit the silent fall-through. Both layers point to the same behavior. Why no description change: the F007 features.json description already said 'p0 from existing plan.tier=p0, interactive from --mode flag or JARVIS_RUN_MODE env' — accurate to the lock. The bug was implementation drift, not framing.

question: F022 OSS readiness: lock the implementation scope before writing code. Apache-2.0 license, sanitization approach, CI surface, doctor failure mode, and acceptance split — what gets shipped in this slice?
answer: Locked with five guardrails: (D-A) License: Apache-2.0 only. Top-level LICENSE file, no NOTICE unless notice-bearing third-party material is actually present. Vendored licenses preserved under claude/skills/.../vendor where they exist. (D-B) Sanitization is hybrid-strict, not 'document live defaults': side-effecting scripts (bootstrap.sh, firebase_client.py) require JARVIS_FIREBASE_PROJECT/--project and JARVIS_BILLING_ACCOUNT/--billing-account explicitly — no campaign defaults. environments.json + .firebaserc untracked, .example templates committed, generated by bootstrap.sh. Plan dirs and tests retain historical IDs (audit/evidence integrity). Campaign-convenience scripts (refresh-costs.sh) keep their hardcoded billing project, allowed via .env.local + the sanitization_check allowlist. (D-C) CI includes ruff check + ruff format --check + Pydantic schema imports + pytest + sanitization_check + bootstrap.sh preflight tests. No allowed-failure jobs: existing ruff debt was cleared (121 auto-fixes + 3 manual + 44 format passes) rather than scoped around. pyproject.toml configures a curated rule set (E/F/W/I/UP/B) with claude/shared excluded as vendored. (D-D) jarvis_doctor aborts on any red with remediation; never warns-and-continues. Acceptance is split: REQUIRED for F022 flip = local CI-equivalent green (pytest 182, ruff clean, sanitization clean, bootstrap.sh syntax + arg-validation tests, jarvis_doctor green on this repo, simulated doctor failure paths covered). OPTIONAL = real clean-GCP-project bootstrap smoke; if not run in this slice, marked as post-merge manual validation, not a blocker. (Guardrail) SA key generation is opt-in via --create-key only, with explicit warning printed AND .gitignore + git check-ignore verification before any write — long-lived keys are too dangerous for an implicit default.
rationale: Why Apache-2.0 not MIT: explicit patent grant matters for a project that bundles IP-bearing prompt templates, schema designs, and conventions; MIT silence on patents is a known gap. Why no NOTICE without justification: empty NOTICE files are a maintenance liability (engineers add bogus entries 'just in case' and the file rots); only create one when something actually requires it. Why hybrid-strict sanitization: 'documented live defaults' is a smell — it claims safety while shipping a foot-gun. Removing the campaign default from side-effecting paths makes accidental deployment to the maintainer's project structurally impossible, which is what 'open source' means in this context. Plan dirs keep historical IDs because the audit trail is the value; rewriting them would falsify the historical record and break agent-conventions audit-chain assumptions. Why no allowed-failure CI: a lint job that's allowed to fail is worse than no lint job — it trains the team to ignore CI red. Better to do the cleanup once. Why curated ruff rule set instead of 'select = ALL': we can expand later cheaply; starting too broad is what produces the allowed-failure trap. Why doctor aborts on red: the user just paid (in mental model and time) to install this; a partial green that 'mostly works' guarantees a confused first-day debugging session. Loud failure with remediation is faster to fix. Why split the acceptance: the original spec required 'fresh clone on a clean machine' as a flip blocker. That's a real human action that can't be automated in CI without provisioning a real clean GCP project (~$0 but real billing exposure and ~10 minutes wallclock). Splitting lets the slice ship on machine-verifiable evidence while flagging the human-only validation as a post-merge step. Why explicit --create-key: SA keys are the credential most likely to leak (they're long-lived, broadly-scoped, and accidentally check-in-able). Making creation explicit + loud + gitignore-verified is cheap insurance against the worst-case incident.

Sanitized in-place: storage.rules, firestore.rules, plan_target.py docstring, smoke_test_storage.py docstring, firebase_client.py (constants → required-env-var functions). Cleared in one pass per the lock. (3) `.firebaserc` had to be untracked too (carried jarvis-a6ee1 as the orchestrator alias) — added to gitignore with .example template, generated by bootstrap.sh same as environments.json. (b) Dependency requirements not yet pinned — pyproject.toml only configures ruff; future slice should add a pinned requirements.txt or [project] table. (c) shellcheck not added to CI; bootstrap.sh validated only via bash -n + behavioral preflight tests. Tests passing: 182 (existing 149 + 33 new). Ruff: clean. Format: clean. rationale: Why log the surprises: this is an open-source slice, and the failure modes encountered (content-filter on COC, ruff debt revealing format-never-ran, .firebaserc-shaped sanitization holes, self-matching grep) are exactly the kinds of pitfalls a future contributor or fork-and-deploy operator will hit. Recording them in decisions.jsonl rather than in commit messages keeps them queryable when someone re-runs the bootstrap on a new project. Why split D076 (lock) and D077 (results): the lock was a contract before code was written; the results entry validates the contract held + records what shifted. Splitting preserves the pre/post integrity of the decisions log. Why pinning + shellcheck land in a future slice: they're scope creep in F022 (CI hygiene, not OSS readiness per se) and the lock said 'no half-finished implementations' — pinning the dependency tree properly is a separate decision (pip-tools vs uv vs requirements + constraints).

question: F022 review surfaced four blockers and a medium finding after the initial flip. What were they, and what did the fixes look like?
answer: Four blockers and one medium, all valid: (1) bootstrap.sh --dry-run was not a real dry-run — auth probes ran before any output; the SA-existence describe call ran unconditionally; the IAM-binding loop redirected `run`'s echo to /dev/null. (2) jarvis_doctor's '15/15 green' claim in D077 was machine-dependent — on an unauthenticated machine it shows 13/15 with gcloud-auth + firebase-auth red. (3) Sanitization was a false green: scripts/refresh-costs.sh kept its allowlist entry while still containing the campaign billing project + a billing-account ID in a comment, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md still embedded the maintainer's personal email — the sanitization_check only checked project ID + billing account, never email or noreply identity. (4) bootstrap omitted roles/logging.logWriter from the SA bindings (F002 included it) and used roles/storage.objectAdmin (narrower than the original storage.admin) without documenting the choice. Medium: the existing dry-run test allowed the script to die on auth as long as billing format passed — exactly the behavior the acceptance was meant to prevent. Fixes: (1) Wrapped auth checks in `if ! $DRY_RUN`. Added a `quiet_run` helper that echoes always and only suppresses real-run stdout, replacing the broken `run ... >/dev/null` pattern. Added a `probe` helper that returns 1 in dry-run so describe-then-create branches print the create command. Confirmed with a fresh dry-run output that all six steps + four IAM bindings echo, zero side effects fire. (2) Added `--skip-auth` flag to jarvis_doctor that omits gcloud-auth + firebase-auth checks; rewrote the F022 acceptance to explicitly state structural-checks-green-on-any-clone vs full-checks-green-in-an-authenticated-environment as separate criteria. CI workflow simplified to call `--skip-auth` directly instead of post-filtering JSON. README + CONTRIBUTING document the flag. Added two doctor tests: `test_skip_auth_omits_auth_checks` (asserts the auth result rows are present in full mode and absent under skip_auth) and `test_skip_auth_propagates_through_main` (asserts argparse → run_all_checks plumbing). (3) Moved scripts/refresh-costs.sh under scripts/maintainer/ + gitignored that whole directory + removed the allowlist entry. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md now points reporters at GitHub private security advisories (and CONTRIBUTING.md as fallback contact path). sanitization_check.py grew a third pattern (the maintainer username, assembled from parts so the script doesn't self-match) which catches @gmail, @silexr.com, and the GitHub noreply form. The check still scans 277 tracked files and exits 0 — but the surface is real now. (4) Added roles/logging.logWriter to the SA binding loop. Wrote a 6-line comment block above the loop documenting the storage.objectAdmin-not-storage.admin choice as deliberate least-privilege (the smoke test only needs upload + signed URL). (Medium) Replaced the lenient test with `test_dry_run_executes_zero_side_effects` that asserts returncode 0, all six step headers present, all four IAM-binding commands echoed, and no auth-failure messages in stderr. Also tightened `test_billing_account_format_accepts_standard_shape` into the new positive test rather than a 'doesn't reject the shape' check. Final tally: 186 tests passing (was 182 + 4 new); ruff + format + sanitization clean; doctor 13/13 under --skip-auth; bootstrap dry-run produces a complete preview with zero cloud calls.
rationale: Why each blocker was actually a blocker, not a nit: (a) Dry-run that authenticates is the canonical sharp-edge bug for bootstrap scripts — anyone who runs --dry-run on a clean machine hits an auth abort and assumes the script is broken, never seeing the preview that would have helped them. The fix had to make --dry-run truly side-effect-free. (b) D077 claiming 15/15 was a textbook 'works on my machine' artifact: I conflated my authenticated state with the repo's structural correctness. The acceptance should never depend on whether the maintainer happens to be logged in. Splitting structural vs operational checks via --skip-auth makes the contract honest: CI can run it, fresh clones can run it, the maintainer can run the full version. (c) The sanitization_check scope was tight only against the named patterns. An allowlist entry on a script that contains other leak-shaped tokens (billing IDs, app categorization mapping the maintainer's product portfolio) is exactly the false-green the lock said to avoid. Moving it under scripts/maintainer/ + gitignore is the clean answer: this script is genuinely operator-private, and pretending otherwise via allowlist is what made the original check dishonest. The expanded pattern set (project + billing + maintainer username) closes the foot-gun for future contributors who might paste an email into a non-plan file. (d) Logs Writer omission would have surfaced as a runtime error the first time the orchestrator tried to write structured logs from production — much worse than fixing it in setup. storage.objectAdmin vs storage.admin is a real least-privilege improvement worth keeping, but it has to be documented or a reviewer reasonably reads the deviation as accidental. Why the medium matters: a test that codifies the wrong contract is worse than no test — it tells future contributors the broken behavior is intentional. Replacing it with the right contract removes the false reassurance.

question: Second-pass F022 review surfaced three more issues after D078. What were they, and what shifted in the contract?
answer: Three valid findings: (1) jarvis_doctor --skip-auth was not actually green on a fresh clone — check_secrets_dir hard-failed if .secrets/ didn't exist, and .secrets/ is gitignored so a fresh GitHub checkout never has it. The maintainer's worktree happens to have an untracked .secrets/, which is why local runs were green and the D078 claim of 'fresh-clone safe' was unverified. CI runs --skip-auth at .github/workflows/ci.yml:47, so this would have been caught only on first PR. (2) README still pointed at scripts/refresh-costs.sh in three places (quickstart step 4, project layout, money-monitoring section) even though refresh-costs.sh was moved under scripts/maintainer/ + gitignored. After commit, OSS docs would tell users to run a script that doesn't exist in the public surface. (3) sanitization_check used `git ls-files` which only lists tracked + cached files — untracked-not-ignored files (the F022 artifacts before staging) were never scanned, so the green result was scoped to the wrong set. Fixes: (1) Rewrote check_secrets_dir to make existence optional. The security invariant is 'if .secrets/ exists, git ignores it' — a missing dir on a fresh clone is fine, and bootstrap --create-key creates it on demand. The check now distinguishes three states: missing+gitignored (green, 'not present yet'), missing+not-gitignored (red, 'add it before --create-key'), and present+not-gitignored (red, the catastrophic case, with 'leaking SA keys' remediation). Added three tests against tmp_path-built mini git repos covering each path. Updated F022 acceptance to explicitly state 'fresh clone (no .secrets/ yet, no authenticated CLIs)' as the green target. (2) Removed the entire 'Configure billing tracking' step from quickstart. Renumbered subsequent steps (was 4-6, now 4-5). Replaced the project-layout listing of refresh-costs.sh with the OSS-relevant scripts (bootstrap.sh, jarvis_doctor.py, sanitization_check.py, quota_check.py). Rewrote the money-monitoring table to flag GCP $ refresh as 'operator-supplied; not bundled' and removed the silexr-billing reference. (3) Switched `tracked_files()` from `git ls-files` to `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, which scans tracked + staged + untracked-not-ignored. File count went 277 → 290 (picked up the 13 untracked F022 artifacts: pyproject.toml, scripts/bootstrap.sh, scripts/jarvis_doctor.py, scripts/sanitization_check.py, scripts/maintainer/.gitkeep, scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_f022_*.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml, etc.). All 10 sanitization tests still pass; 0 leaks across the expanded set. Final state: 187 tests passing (was 186 + 1 net new for the secrets-dir contract), ruff + format + sanitization clean, doctor 13/13 under --skip-auth on a synthetic fresh clone, plan validates.
rationale: Why each finding was actually a contract violation: (a) D077 first claimed '15/15 green' on the maintainer's authenticated machine; D078 fixed that by adding --skip-auth and claiming '13/13 green'; this review found that '13/13' was ALSO machine-dependent because of the untracked .secrets/ leak. The pattern: I kept asserting green on properties of *my* worktree rather than properties of *a fresh clone*. The fix isn't another claim — it's a structural change so the green result follows from repo state alone. The new check encodes the actual security invariant (gitignore protection) rather than the proxy invariant (directory existence). (b) Stale doc references after a file move are the kind of thing CI cannot catch without a link checker. The honest fix is to remove the references entirely and reframe the cost-tracking story as 'operator-supplied'. Doing it as 'maintainer-private; see scripts/maintainer/' would tell readers about a directory we just gitignored, which is at best confusing and at worst a leakage signal ('what's in there?'). (c) `git ls-files` defaulting to cached-only is the kind of intuitive-looking subtlety that bites once. The reviewer correctly noted that pre-staging sanitization is exactly when leaks are most likely (a freshly-written file might still have placeholder text the author forgot to replace). Switching to `--cached --others --exclude-standard` makes the check 'scan everything that would land in `git add .`' which is the operator's actual concern. Why not just '--others' alone: ignored files (.secrets/, scripts/maintainer/) MUST stay excluded — they contain real campaign data and are deliberately out of the OSS surface. `--exclude-standard` enforces that. Why I'm continuing to log every revision rather than amending D077/D078: the decision-log audit chain is the most valuable thing in docs/plans/ — falsifying it (rewriting earlier entries to match later understanding) would defeat its purpose. Future readers should be able to see the progression of review findings, not a sanitized final state.
